content: Great work! Seems that it only support the original CommonMark with table and tasklist extension, but no special code handling LaTeX formulas (in fact originally doc-gen4 uses CommonMark C library for rendering markdown, but it does not have special code handling LaTeX formulas, which breaks some _ inside $ ... $, so later it is switched to md4c). Otherwise I think it's possible to use your library to replace my https://github.com/acmepjz/md4lean in doc-gen4

Thanks!

You're right, it's currently CommonMark and GFM only.

Is there a specification anywhere for the LaTeX formula handling?
The nice thing about markdown standards is there's so many to choose from (but most of them are not written down anywhere)

Yup, I've been doing some digging and there definitely seems to be little consensus on what "correct" means here.

I guess I'll just mirror md4c given that that seems to work for Lean as things currently stand :shrug:

Paul Butcher said:

Is there a specification anywhere for the LaTeX formula handling?

I don't think so; maybe it is merely "the things between $ ... $ and $$ ... $$ are not parsed as Markdown, but leave them as-is, so that mathjax or katex can handle them correctly". The problem is how to locate reliably the beginning and the ending of a formula.

Paul Butcher said:

I guess I'll just mirror md4c

Seems that md4c and GFM diverges on certain table syntax (l've read them in the issues of md4c).
16 messages were moved here from #Project announcements > Lean implementation of Markdown by Chris Henson.

Hmm. I've just taken a look, and you're right that GFM and md4c differ significantly in how they handle tables.

And it's broader than that, md4c also differs significantly in how autolinking works, and then has a few minor differences around whitespace handling (potentially important for code spans) and strikethrough.

And then it supports a couple of things that aren't in GFM at all: wikilinks and underline.

@Jz Pan to what extent might any of the above be an issue for how markdown is used in doc-gen4?

I don't think we use wikilink feature in doc-gen4 at all (maybe you can check mathlib?). I'm not sure underline, strikethrough, etc. But maybe these are minor issues. Also for tables, I don't think we used any tables in mathlib docs, complex enough to trigger differences of these two implementations.

The feature we actually used is: LaTeX formula handling, and standard Markdown citing feature (we first inject all bibliography entries as a preamble of Markdown, so that if docstring cites any of them, they will appear in the rendered HTML and we postprocess them to link to correct place). The others are not that important I think; we can always plug it into doc-gen4 and fix bugs if they appear.

Paul Butcher said:

formal safety

So did you proved that it never allows HTML injection?

Assuming you mean Link reference definitions then yes, they are supported.

And yes, it proves absence of HTML injection as long as you use renderHtmlSafe; there's also renderHtml for situations where you want HTML passthrough (which is standard CommonMark).

The relevant theorems are here (for CommonMark) and here for GFM.

Oh another thing is that currently doc-gen4 requires that the generated HTML from markdown is XHTML compatible (i.e. a valid XML) since there are postprocessing code assuming it is XML. An alternative approach is postprocess the AST directly.
... which means that <p> must ends with </p>, and use <br/>, etc. etc.
Ah! Good to know. That’s definitely not the case at the moment; lean-html (which lean-markdown builds upon) only outputs HTML at the moment. It should be easy enough to add an XML option though.

@Jz Pan I've just pushed changes which add md4c-style LaTeX support:

https://github.com/paulbutcher/lean-markdown

I've added tests which run examples through md4c to confirm that the behaviour is identical (with one exception mentioned in KNOWN_ISSUES.md).

I was already closer to XHTML than I remembered because the existing CommonMark test corpus uses self-closing tags, but I've updated it to be fully XHTML throughout.

The output is <span class="math inline"> or <span class="math display">, which differs from md4c's <x-equation>: let me know if that will be a problem.

I've also taken the opportunity to update the comments around the theorems in the library: they did, I believe, prove what they were intended to prove, but it wasn't always immediately clear why. The new comments should, I hope, make them much more self-evident. If you fancy taking a look and convincing yourself that they are doing what I claim, I'd love to hear your thoughts.

Thanks for your effort!

Paul Butcher said:

The output is <span class="math inline"> or <span class="math display">, which differs from md4c's <x-equation>: let me know if that will be a problem.

In fact what doc-gen4 expected is neither span or x-equation. Since it uses MathJax for LaTeX formula rendering, it expects simply $ ... $. The point is don't treat * or _ in math formula as markdown format character, and escape < and & as < and &, etc. I've tested <span class="math inline"> on MathJax official live demo, and it doesn't get recognized.

Oh! Sorry, I completely misunderstood (blush).

To make sure I understand correctly, could you perhaps send me an example of both the input and the associated output you need for your use case?

Sorry but I don't have examples or test cases in md4lean. But I can show you the modification of md4c code to implement this feature:

        case MD_SPAN_LATEXMATH:
            if (r->flags & MD_HTML_FLAG_MATHJAX) {
                if (r->flags & MD_HTML_FLAG_MATHJAX_USE_DOLLAR) RENDER_VERBATIM(r, "$");
                else RENDER_VERBATIM(r, "\\(");
            } else RENDER_VERBATIM(r, "<x-equation>");
            break;
        case MD_SPAN_LATEXMATH_DISPLAY:
            if (r->flags & MD_HTML_FLAG_MATHJAX) {
                if (r->flags & MD_HTML_FLAG_MATHJAX_USE_DOLLAR) RENDER_VERBATIM(r, "$$");
                else RENDER_VERBATIM(r, "\\[");
            } else RENDER_VERBATIM(r, "<x-equation type=\"display\">");
            break;

and

        case MD_SPAN_LATEXMATH:
            if (r->flags & MD_HTML_FLAG_MATHJAX) {
                if (r->flags & MD_HTML_FLAG_MATHJAX_USE_DOLLAR) RENDER_VERBATIM(r, "$");
                else RENDER_VERBATIM(r, "\\)");
            } else RENDER_VERBATIM(r, "</x-equation>");
            break;
        case MD_SPAN_LATEXMATH_DISPLAY:
            if (r->flags & MD_HTML_FLAG_MATHJAX) {
                if (r->flags & MD_HTML_FLAG_MATHJAX_USE_DOLLAR) RENDER_VERBATIM(r, "$$");
                else RENDER_VERBATIM(r, "\\]");
            } else RENDER_VERBATIM(r, "</x-equation>");
            break;

So it just simply replace the HTML tags by $.

Ahh I read your examples and I think your implementation also works for MathJax. In fact you output `<span class="math inline"> together with \( so it is also recognized by MathJax. The span thing got ignored automatically since it's not defined in the CSS I think.

Sorry for the noise!

I've just been playing with MathJax and was just about to say exactly the same thing :stuck_out_tongue_wink:

No problem at all: this is one of those areas where it would be much easier if there were some standards!
Did you tested this: This is *italic* $ This is not *italic* $

Yes. This is what it generates (assuming that math is enabled):

<p>This is <em>italic</em> <span class="math inline">\( This is not *italic* \)</span></p>
Great! I found this test in your test cases.

FYI, there is one area where I know that I diverge from md4c:

https://github.com/paulbutcher/lean-markdown/blob/main/KNOWN_ISSUES.md#4-math-and-emphasis-that-cross-resolve-differently-from-md4c
I read it but I don't think it's an issue.
